reference_memory.normal_pattern: The channel exhibits a robust quasi-periodic pattern with a dominant period of ~91 points, consistent across all candidates. Normal behavior consists of repeating motifs: (1) a sharp positive spike (peak amplitude ~1.0–1.7 robust std) followed by a rapid descent to baseline or below; (2) a flat or gently sloping plateau lasting ~10–20 points; (3) a brief negative dip (~−0.5 to −1.0) often accompanied by small high-frequency oscillations (2–3 sub-peaks); (4) recovery to baseline before the next cycle. Amplitude is tightly bounded: 90th-percentile absolute amplitude ≈2.04 robust std, with MAD ≈0.67–0.68 across candidates. Baseline level varies modestly (median from −0.015 to +0.32), but local trends are near-zero (slope per point ≤±0.0022). Curvature is generally low except in candidate 0 and 3 where slight convex/concave drift appears over multi-cycle spans—likely due to slow baseline shifts rather than true trend. Noise manifests as small-amplitude (<0.3) jagged fluctuations within plateaus or dips, not as independent spikes; isolated high-frequency bursts (e.g., 3–4 consecutive tiny peaks) are part of normal morphology when embedded in a dip. Boundary truncation is minimal; all intervals are cleanly cut at cycle boundaries. Acceptable variation includes ±0.3 shift in median level, occasional extra sub-peak in dips, and minor asymmetry in spike rise/fall times—but never sustained monotonic drift, double-peaked main spikes, or prolonged flat segments >30 points without any inflection.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer candidate 2 for queries with stable baseline and high motif fidelity; use candidate 0 for queries matching zero-baseline single-cycle patterns; select candidate 1 when query shows mild negative drift or a prominent high spike; choose candidate 3 for longer windows (>3 cycles) or when query exhibits gentle positive slope. Avoid using candidate 0 alone for multi-cycle inference—its lack of dip oscillations is an artifact of short window, not abnormality.
uncertainties: Exact phase alignment of spikes across cycles is not fully constrained—small phase jitter (~±3 pts) may be normal
Whether double-spike clusters (candidate 3) are always normal or occasionally anomalous requires query validation
Baseline offset magnitude (−0.01 to +0.33) may reflect sensor calibration drift rather than true process change; treat offsets as permissible unless abrupt
High-frequency oscillations in dips could be noise or structured dynamics; current evidence supports inclusion in normal pattern
